html:
Mwezi IV Gisabo was king of Burundi for about half a century until his death in 1908, the last to rule an independent kingdom.

He came to the throne young and spent much of his reign fighting rival princes, and he held off slave traders from the east coast. When German forces arrived in the 1890s he refused to submit, and they backed his rivals against him.

After German attacks he signed the treaty of Kiganda in 1903, accepting the German protectorate in return for keeping his throne. The Germans then ruled through him, as the Belgians later ruled through his successors. He is remembered as a symbol of resistance in Burundi, and his reign saw the founding of the German post at Usumbura.
